paper_title: A Universal Bound on QCD Axions from Supernovae
suggested_experiment_name: Supernova 1987A cooling bound on QCD axions
coupling_convention: m_a in eV (y-axis) vs f_a in GeV (x-axis). The plot shows the QCD axion parameter space with the red shaded region indicating the 68% C.L. model-independent bound from this work (supernova constraint). The y-axis represents axion mass m_a in eV, and the x-axis represents the axion decay constant f_a in GeV.
notes: Paper derives a new model-independent bound on QCD axion mass from supernova cooling via a previously-overlooked tree-level production channel from shift-symmetry-breaking operators in Chiral Perturbation Theory. The primary result is presented as a bound on the axion decay constant f_a > 1.1^{+0.4}_{-0.6} × 10^8 GeV (68% C.L.), which is equivalent to m_a < 5.3^{+7.3}_{-1.3} × 10^{-2} eV. This is a mass-independent (flat) bound valid across all axion masses well below the supernova core temperature. The bound improves on prior estimates by ~2 orders of magnitude and applies to all QCD axion models solving the strong CP problem, including astrophobic axions with suppressed derivative couplings. The coupling_type is AxionMass because the paper's primary result is on the f_a-m_a plane itself (cosmological/astrophysical bound from SN1987A cooling), not on a coupling constant like g_agamma or g_an. The data_points encode the f_a bound as a horizontal line spanning a wide mass range (sentinel format for mass-independent bounds).
